copy_pick.why: Candidate 3 wears the dry-understatement directive best: 'an unrequested delivery,' 'using their yard,' 'pack a paper map.' It also avoids the recent cards' recycled 'Add…' construction, yesterday's FBI-breach beat and the delayed-train joke, and keeps the focus tightly on the Poland strike.

doom.driver: Ukraine war spilling into NATO territory. The war between Russia and Ukraine once again creeps onto European territory – from attacks on ships to missiles in Poland and fresh allegations of Russian operations inside Denmark.
doom.summary: Russian missiles landed in Poland and NATO is convening, which is what alliances do when the neighbor's war starts using their yard. Meanwhile Ukraine sank a Russian warship that had only stopped in Libya for fuel. Back home, COP31 ended in the longest stalemate in UN climate history, and the DNI is warning Americans to expect more outages over Thanksgiving, so pack a paper map.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: Meta's AI chief says superintelligence is 'arriving' just as the Nasdaq has its worst week since 2020.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: The Nvidia chip scandal now reportedly runs through China's spy agency, and an AI cheating scandal toppled South Korea's education minister.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Missiles in Poland, a Russian warship sunk in a Libyan port, strikes killing at least 15 near Kyiv, and Houthi attacks on Saudi oil.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: Banks are blocking AI agents from customer accounts and safety experts question Tesla's self-driving claims, while Wang says the next year carries 'great consequence'.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Asian regulators are scrambling to support their markets as fears grow that the AI boom is turning into a bust.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. The interior of Copenhagen Airport's Terminal 3 departure hall, after a night of closed airspace. The whole back wall is a floor-to-ceiling glass curtain wall, and it is filled by a huge blood-red and furnace-orange sky. A hellish glare rises from below the horizon and floods the room. Beyond the glass the apron is bathed in furnace-orange light. Grounded white-tailed passenger jets sit nose-in at their gates, and the Kastrup control tower stands as a tall bold silhouette. A Danish flag, a white cross on red, hangs limp from a pole beside the apron. Bruised violet shadows pool on the polished floor, which reflects long streaks of orange. In the foreground, a tired woman in a long winter coat and a small child in a puffy jacket stand whole and small, hand in hand, facing the glass. They are cut into bold flat silhouettes against the blazing sky, and their long shadows stretch back toward the camera. Behind them, rows of stranded travelers slump asleep on benches among rolling suitcases and strollers, all rimmed in orange light. A single abandoned luggage cart stands in the middle of the hall. The mood is menacing and wrong: a busy airport frozen and emptied under a sky that looks like the gates of hell. Everything is clearly visible, with large shapes and strong contrast that read at phone size.

minor: The Danish flag's cross is nearly centered and the flag is washed in orange, so it reads less clearly as a Danish flag.
The seated travelers on both sides are murky, and their limbs blend into the benches and luggage. This is acceptable because it reads as a distant, shadowed crowd.
The jets on the apron are somewhat muddled, with tail fins and fuselages blending into the glare. They are still recognizable as parked planes.
The woman and child are mostly flat dark silhouettes with little detail. They stay clear against the bright sky, and their clasped hands read correctly.
The glass mullions pass in front of the tower and sky in a slightly irregular way. This does not hurt readability.

dawn.driver: A 194-year-old tortoise has a remarkable anti-aging secret hidden in its DNA
dawn.summary: Jonathan the giant tortoise, at 194 the oldest living land animal on Earth, has let researchers read his genome, and they found 287 unique variants tied to DNA repair and inflammation control that may explain his remarkable lifespan. In medicine, a new AI tool spotted hidden signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, catching 85% of cases across nearly 70,000 patients. On the track and the court, Marc Marquez drew level with Giacomo Agostini by winning his eighth premier-class title, and Carlos Alcaraz claimed his first ATP Finals crown.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Brown University chemists showed that Einstein's relativity reshapes how heavy atoms form triple bonds, rewriting a textbook rule, while another team found DNA may carry its own built-in sunscreen that helped early life flourish.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: Kenya and DR Congo agreed to restore diplomatic ties, with both leaders pledging mutual respect for sovereignty.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Parents surveyed by Sesame Workshop say their kids are growing kinder than a decade ago, and Alcaraz joined an exclusive four-man club by adding the ATP Finals to all four majors.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Researchers estimate GLP-1 drugs could reduce food demand enough to free up farmland larger than Italy for nature.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: An AI model that reads subtle patterns in patient records could give doctors a five-year head start on bladder cancer.

copy_pick.why: Candidate 3 best wears the front-page-triumph directive, with one strong verb in 'JONATHAN, 194, UNLOCKS THE LONG-LIFE CODE'; it avoids the overused 'Elsewhere' transition and names specific, purely good stories.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. NIGHT SCENE on the narrow main street of Jamestown, St. Helena, in the small hours before dawn. Steep dark volcanic cliffs rise on both sides under a deep teal-black sky of tiny stars, and a sliver of South Atlantic shows at the far end of the street. Deep shadows dominate. All light comes from artificial sources: two amber cast-iron streetlamps and the glowing windows of a whitewashed Georgian pub with green shutters. In the pub's big front window, an old CRT television glows soft green. On its screen is a huge domed Aldabra tortoise on a sunlit lawn, with a thin golden double helix of tiny light points rising above its shell. Inside, a single elderly islander in a flat cap sits whole on a bar stool, seen from behind and watching the screen, with a warm amber pendant lamp over the bar. Outside on a small iron café table under the nearest streetlamp lies a folded newspaper. Its front page is a large pixel photo of the same tortoise with scribbled gray lines in place of text. Beside it sits a steaming enamel mug. A child's crayon drawing of a green-brown tortoise with a gold spiral shell is taped inside the window glass, catching the amber light. Wet cobblestones reflect pools of amber and green, and the sky at the horizon holds the faintest pale gold. The whole scene feels hushed, warm and quietly hopeful, as though the island is waiting for clarity to arrive.

minor: The newspaper masthead has small letter-like marks that read as pseudo-text. They are tiny and look like scribbles at phone size.
The photo on the newspaper looks more like a green mound or hill with a helix than a clear tortoise.
The elderly man in the window is dark and blends into the bar and chair behind him. He still reads as one seated figure seen from behind.
The tortoise on the TV and the crayon tortoise are simple and a little blobby, but they are recognizable.
